explain.say: In 1405 a fleet of over two hundred ships and about 27,800 men left China under the admiral Zheng He. Over seven voyages it reached Java, Sri Lanka, India, Arabia and East Africa, decades before da Gama. Then the voyages stopped. Look at the timeline of the Ming and Qing dynasties.

explain.say: Follow the map. From near today's Shanghai the fleets sailed past Vietnam and Indonesia to Sri Lanka, India and the coast of Kenya, collecting tribute and gifts like a giraffe for the emperor. After 1433 court officials ended them as costly. Why might a land empire worried about the Mongols turn away from the sea?

items2: Shanghai > Vietnam > Indonesia > Sri Lanka > India > Kenya
draw.label: Zheng He's voyages, 1405 to 1433

explain.say: Now look at the Single Whip reform of 1581: most taxes were to be paid in silver. That pulled in silver from Japan and the Americas, through Manila. Many historians link the Ming collapse partly to slowing silver imports and failed harvests in the cold 1630s. Rebels took Beijing in 1644 and Manchu armies from the north-east swept in. What does a tax system have to do with world trade?

explain.say: The Manchu Qing dynasty doubled the territory, adding Taiwan, Mongolia, Xinjiang and Tibet. See the sizes: from about 60 million registered in 1393 to roughly 300 million by 1800. New crops from the Americas, like maize and sweet potato, helped feed them. Why might fast growth bring problems later?

draw.text: Figures are rough; early counts missed many people.

explain.say: Were the Qing simply Chinese emperors? See the debate. Ping-ti Ho stressed sinicisation; New Qing historians like Evelyn Rawski and Mark Elliott show emperors who stayed Manchu and ruled Mongols and Tibetans differently. Great work. Exam tip: link China to world silver and crops, not just dynasties.

draw.verdict: Both: Chinese emperor and Inner Asian khan.

faq.q: Why did Zheng He's voyages stop?
faq.a: After 1433 the Ming court ended them: they were very costly, officials opposed the eunuch-led expeditions, and the state's priorities turned to defending the northern frontier against the Mongols.
asks: How far did Zheng He sail?

faq.q: What was the Single Whip reform?
faq.a: A Ming tax reform, applied empire-wide by 1581 under Zhang Juzheng, that combined many taxes and labour duties into a single payment in silver. It tied China's economy to imported silver from Japan and the Americas.
asks: Why did the Ming collect taxes in silver?

faq.q: How did the Qing conquer China?
faq.a: In 1644 rebels under Li Zicheng took Beijing and the last Ming emperor died. The Ming general Wu Sangui let Manchu forces through the Great Wall at Shanhai Pass; they took Beijing and over decades conquered the south.
asks: Why did the Ming dynasty fall?

faq.q: Why did China's population grow so fast under the Qing?
faq.a: Long internal peace, new land, and American crops like maize and sweet potatoes that grew on hillsides helped the population rise to roughly 300 million by 1800, though estimates vary.
asks: How many people lived in Qing China?

faq.q: What is the New Qing History?
faq.a: An approach from the 1990s, associated with Evelyn Rawski and Mark Elliott, that uses Manchu-language sources to show the Qing as an Inner Asian empire whose rulers kept a distinct Manchu identity, not simply as sinicised Chinese emperors.

facts: The Ming dynasty ruled from 1368 to 1644 and the Qing from 1644 to 1912.
Zheng He led seven voyages between 1405 and 1433.
The Forbidden City in Beijing was completed in 1420.

quiz.say: What did the Single Whip reform require?
quiz.show: The Single Whip reform made taxes payable in…
quiz.why: Combining taxes into silver payments linked China to world silver supplies.

wrong.1: Grain taxes were largely converted to silver.
wrong.2: Ming paper money had lost value; silver replaced it.

quiz.say: China grew from about 150 million people in 1600 to about 300 million in 1800. By what factor did it grow?
quiz.why: 300 divided by 150 is 2, so the population doubled.

wrong.2: Ten percent growth would give only 165 million.
